label: heads the record calls WHOLE and still gives a stem direction
what: docs/engraving-conventions.md [C9 + L10] excludes whole notes throughout - a semibreve carries no stem. The registry files it ASSERTED WITH NO FIGURE. A contradiction has two readings and only the print separates them: the head is really WHOLE (the DIRECTION is false, and the convention holds) or it is really a HALF note (the CLASS is false and the convention is not what failed).
headline: NOT ONE of the 17 adjudicated heads is a whole note whose direction is the false claim. In 16 of 17 the CLASS is false — the box holds a staff-line gap (5), a time-signature digit 8 (8), a dotted HALF note with a printed stem (2), or a hairpin wedge (1). So this population is a `notehead_class` false-positive population and NOT a convention failure: the convention is neither contradicted nor confirmed by it.
method_warning: ⚠️ AT TILE MAGNIFICATION I READ TWO OF THESE WRONG AND THE WIDE STRIP CORRECTED BOTH — a time-signature digit 8 and a dotted half note both read as `a hollow head with no stem`. A crop centred on a head cannot tell you the head is a NUMERAL. Every verdict here rests on a full-width strip or a 4x zoom, never on the tile alone.
